channel.title: CoreForge — dMAT news & updates
channel.description: Curated dMAT and APS India updates. CoreForge is an unofficial practice platform — every entry links to its official source.

item.title: First-cycle dMAT certificates issued from 12 October 2026
item.description:
Certificates for the first India cycle are issued from 12 October 2026 and are downloaded from the g.a.s.t. participant portal. Core and the subject module are scored separately — percentile rank plus a standardised dMAT score from 0–200 with mean 100 — and the total is the sum of the two. The certificate is valid indefinitely. The dMAT result appears on the APS certificate; for affected applicants the APS certificate is only issued after the dMAT certificate is submitted.
Source: aps-india.de/dmat — APS India — https://aps-india.de/dmat/ (as of 2026-08-07)

item.title: First India dMAT test date: 26 September 2026
item.description:
The first India dMAT is sat on 26 September 2026. A sitting is the Core Module plus exactly one subject module and runs about 3.5 hours including a 30-minute break. It is digital, at licensed test centers; single-choice throughout — and it is sat in English. No note-taking is allowed anywhere in the exam. Unanswered counts as wrong; no penalty for guessing is documented — never leave blanks.
Read the format guide: https://goldensdmat.in/dmat-info
Source: d-mat.de — official site home (no per-announcement permalink is published) — https://www.d-mat.de/en/ (as of 2026-08-07)

item.title: Registration closes 15 September 2026 for the first India dMAT cycle
item.description:
15 September 2026 is the last day to register for the first India dMAT cycle, which is sat on 26 September 2026. Booking runs through the g.a.s.t. portal, not through APS India, and the fee is €150. The dMAT binds you if your previous degree falls under Engineering, Commerce / Accounting / Finance / Economics, Business / Management and you are filing APS applications for the Summer Semester 2027 intake and all later intakes, and APS will not issue your certificate until your dMAT certificate has been submitted. No second cycle has been announced, so do not plan around one.
Book a slot at gast.de: https://www.gast.de/portal/center-search/center-search/dmat/exams/worldwide?lang=en
Source: gast.de — the official dMAT booking portal — https://www.gast.de/portal/center-search/center-search/dmat/exams/worldwide?lang=en (as of 2026-08-07)

item.title: Brain Gym, subject skills and an index of outside material
item.description:
CoreForge has added a Brain Gym: short seeded drills for the speed, attention, memory and reasoning the Core Module leans on, with one round of the day playable without an account and levels 1 to 3 of every engine on the Free plan. Practice now keeps a streak, a level and a few daily goals; all of it is optional, and calm mode turns every animation off without costing you any of the progress. A missed question in a subject module points at the idea behind it and offers a drill on that topic alone, rather than an explanation of that one item and nothing more. An index of outside material collects links to videos and pages other people published at no charge, each one checked before it was listed and re-checked on a schedule. None of this is official dMAT preparation, and gym points are their own thing — they never touch the practice leaderboard.
Open Brain Gym: https://goldensdmat.in/brain-gym
Source: CoreForge (goldensdmat.in) — our own changelog, not an official dMAT source — https://goldensdmat.in/ (as of 2026-09-06)

item.title: The Free plan replaces the trial: Core Module practice for every account
item.description:
CoreForge no longer has a trial clock: every account is on the Free plan — the Core Module, Figure Sequences, Mathematical Equations and Latin Squares, in practice mode at easy difficulty in 3-question sets, plus its own results, answer review and history — with no card and no expiry. Everything else — the full timed Core Module, the General Academic Module and every subject module, other difficulties and set sizes, mock exams, Learn, analytics, weekly leagues and the AI tutor — is CoreForge Pro at ₹299 a month or ₹1,999 a year, auto-renewing until you cancel in one tap. Accounts that were on the trial are now on the Free plan, and anyone who has already paid keeps full access until their current period ends. The demo drill stays open without an account, capped at 10 questions a day. CoreForge is unofficial practice material and is not affiliated with g.a.s.t., the TestDaF-Institut, APS India or the DAAD.
See what the Free plan includes: https://goldensdmat.in/pricing
Source: CoreForge (goldensdmat.in) — our own changelog, not an official dMAT source — https://goldensdmat.in/ (as of 2026-08-21)

item.title: CoreForge Pro: a free 7-day trial, then ₹299 a month
item.description:
CoreForge is now a paid product. Every module, unlimited practice, full mocks and analytics sit behind one subscription — ₹299 a month or ₹1,999 a year — and every new account starts with a free 7-day trial. CoreForge is unofficial practice material and is not affiliated with g.a.s.t., the TestDaF-Institut, APS India or the DAAD.

item.title: Every published dMAT subject module is now on CoreForge
item.description:
CoreForge now covers every published dMAT subject module, not only the General Academic Module: Computer Science and Data Science, plus all 5 Battery Science tracks (Chemistry, Physics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering). The dMAT is always the Core Module plus exactly one subject module, so sit the one your target programme asks for — the module pages name the programme and, where an institution is published, the university (RWTH Aachen University and Georg-August-Universität Göttingen). Where no official preparatory material exists — currently Data Science — the format here is a documented reconstruction and the app labels it modeled rather than official.
Browse the modules: https://goldensdmat.in/modules
Source: CoreForge (goldensdmat.in) — our own changelog, not an official dMAT source — https://goldensdmat.in/ (as of 2026-08-07)

item.title: GAM practice now spans all 8 official topic areas
item.description:
Every official General Academic Module topic area — mathematics, computational sciences, natural sciences, engineering, business administration, economics, social sciences, humanities — now has its own passages with a real difficulty spread rather than a single sampler. Every passage keeps the official shape: a reading passage followed by single-choice questions — exactly 4 options, exactly 1 correct. Every question goes through the same validator the app runs on AI-generated content: exactly four options with one correct, no duplicated options, and explanations that cite what an option says instead of its letter. Official sample questions do not necessarily reflect the difficulty level of the real test.
Practise the GAM: https://goldensdmat.in/gam
Source: CoreForge (goldensdmat.in) — our own changelog, not an official dMAT source — https://goldensdmat.in/ (as of 2026-08-07)

item.title: Official GAM preparatory materials updated (as at 7 July 2026)
item.description:
g.a.s.t. republished the General Academic Module preparatory materials with an as-at date of 7 July 2026. Passages, questions, and options may contain figures, tables, and formulas. The caveats printed on the material itself are worth taking literally. Official sample questions do not necessarily reflect the difficulty level of the real test. The published topics represent only a selection. CoreForge's GAM content was re-checked against this revision.
Source: d-mat.de — official site home (no per-announcement permalink is published) — https://www.d-mat.de/en/ (as of 2026-08-07)

item.title: dMAT becomes part of APS India for Summer Semester 2027 intakes
item.description:
APS India published version 1.0 of its List of Affected Previous Degree Fields on 29 June 2026, and with it the dMAT became part of the APS procedure — it applies to APS applications for the Summer Semester 2027 intake and all later intakes. Applicants whose previous degree falls under Engineering, Commerce / Accounting / Finance / Economics, Business / Management are covered; Bachelor's applicants, PhD applicants, officially confirmed exchange, partnership, or double-degree programme participants are not. The published exemptions are all anchored to this same date: APS online registration completed before 29 June 2026; complete APS documents shipped before 29 June 2026; an APS certificate already held. The dMAT result appears on the APS certificate; for affected applicants the APS certificate is only issued after the dMAT certificate is submitted. A low score does NOT automatically deny the APS certificate — universities decide how to use the score in admissions.
Check whether your degree is affected: https://goldensdmat.in/dmat-info
Source: aps-india.de/dmat — APS India — https://aps-india.de/dmat/ (as of 2026-08-07)

item.title: First India registration window opens — €150 fee
item.description:
Booking for the first India dMAT cycle opened on 29 June 2026 and runs to 15 September 2026, at a fee of €150. Slots are booked through the g.a.s.t. portal and the test is sat at a licensed test centre. The window covers the whole first cycle, whose test date is 26 September 2026. No later cycle had been announced when this entry was last checked.
Open the booking portal: https://www.gast.de/portal/center-search/center-search/dmat/exams/worldwide?lang=en
Source: gast.de — the official dMAT booking portal — https://www.gast.de/portal/center-search/center-search/dmat/exams/worldwide?lang=en (as of 2026-08-07)
